gaps.concept: True labor causes progressive cervical dilation or effacement; Braxton Hicks contractions do not.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes painful contractions that establish labor from false labor.

gaps.concept: Bishop score combines dilation, effacement, fetal station, cervical consistency, and cervical position; station zero is at the ischial spines.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets a cervical examination before induction.

gaps.concept: Active labor begins around 6 cm dilation; active-phase arrest requires no cervical change despite adequate contractions.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes slow latent labor from true arrest.

gaps.concept: Cephalopelvic disproportion or persistent occiput-posterior position can prevent descent despite adequate uterine contractions.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies a cause of second-stage arrest when contractions are adequate.

gaps.concept: External Doppler records fetal heart rate and a tocodynamometer records contractions; internal scalp electrodes and pressure catheters require ruptured membranes.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies monitoring equipment and when internal monitoring is possible.

gaps.concept: A reactive nonstress test after 32 weeks has at least two fetal heart accelerations of 15 beats/minute for 15 seconds within 20 minutes.
gaps.why_tested: Classifies an antepartum fetal surveillance tracing.

gaps.concept: Biophysical profile scores fetal breathing, movement, tone, amniotic fluid, and nonstress testing; each component receives zero or two points.
gaps.why_tested: Interprets an ultrasound and fetal monitoring score.

gaps.concept: Normal fetal heart baseline is 110–160/min with moderate variability; absent variability plus recurrent decelerations or bradycardia is category III.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes a tracing concerning for fetal acidemia.

gaps.concept: A sinusoidal fetal heart tracing is associated with severe fetal anemia.
gaps.why_tested: Links a distinctive smooth, wave-like tracing to its cause.

gaps.concept: Uterine tachysystole is more than five contractions per 10 minutes and can follow oxytocin or prostaglandin administration.
gaps.why_tested: Explains fetal heart abnormalities during induction.

gaps.concept: Oxytocin activates Gq-linked receptors to raise myometrial intracellular calcium; prolonged high-dose exposure can cause water retention and hyponatremia.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the induction drug’s mechanism or an adverse-effect vignette.

gaps.concept: Misoprostol increases uterine rupture risk in patients with a prior cesarean scar.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies an unsafe cervical-ripening drug in a scarred uterus.

gaps.concept: Ruptured membranes cause vaginal fluid pooling, positive ferning, and alkaline nitrazine testing.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes amniotic fluid leakage from urine or ordinary discharge.

gaps.concept: Intraamniotic infection presents during labor with maternal fever, uterine tenderness, and fetal tachycardia, often after prolonged membrane rupture.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the cause of fever and fetal tachycardia during labor.

gaps.concept: Maternal group B streptococcal colonization warrants intrapartum penicillin to prevent early neonatal infection.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the purpose and timing of antibiotic prophylaxis during delivery.

gaps.concept: Umbilical cord prolapse after membrane rupture, especially with breech or an unengaged presenting part, causes sudden fetal bradycardia.
gaps.why_tested: Explains abrupt fetal deterioration immediately after the membranes rupture.

gaps.concept: Uterine rupture is associated with a prior uterine scar and presents with sudden pain, fetal bradycardia, and loss of fetal station.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes rupture from ordinary labor pain or slow progression.

gaps.concept: Shoulder dystocia may produce the turtle sign; McRoberts positioning with suprapubic pressure is the initial maneuver.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes an impacted shoulder after delivery of the head.

gaps.concept: A boggy uterus indicates uterine atony; overdistension, prolonged labor, and intraamniotic infection increase its risk.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies the cause of heavy bleeding immediately after delivery.

gaps.concept: Persistent postpartum bleeding with a firm, contracted uterus suggests cervical or vaginal laceration.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes genital tract trauma from uterine atony.

gaps.concept: Obstetric disseminated intravascular coagulation causes bleeding from puncture sites, thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT/PTT, and low fibrinogen.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies coagulopathy as the cause of postpartum hemorrhage.

gaps.concept: Placenta accreta results from deficient decidua basalis, often after prior cesarean delivery, and causes failure of placental separation with hemorrhage.
gaps.why_tested: Explains a retained, adherent placenta during the third stage.

gaps.concept: Uterine inversion causes severe postpartum hemorrhage and shock with an absent palpable fundus, often after excessive cord traction.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies a third-stage complication from the abdominal and pelvic examination.

gaps.concept: Amniotic fluid embolism causes sudden hypoxia, hypotension, and disseminated intravascular coagulation during or immediately after delivery.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes abrupt cardiopulmonary collapse from isolated postpartum hemorrhage.

gaps.concept: Accidental dural puncture during epidural placement causes a postpartum headache that worsens upright and improves supine.
gaps.why_tested: Explains a positional headache following labor analgesia.

gaps.concept: Postpartum endometritis is usually polymicrobial and presents with fever, uterine tenderness, and foul lochia, especially after cesarean delivery.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes uterine infection from normal postpartum discharge.

gaps.concept: Lactational mastitis commonly involves Staphylococcus aureus and causes fever with a tender, wedge-shaped erythematous breast area.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes mastitis from uncomplicated breast engorgement.

gaps.concept: Severe postpartum hemorrhage can infarct the enlarged anterior pituitary, causing low prolactin, failure to lactate, and later amenorrhea.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies Sheehan syndrome from its mechanism and hormone pattern.

gaps.concept: Postpartum thyroiditis is painless autoimmune thyroid inflammation; destructive thyrotoxicosis may precede hypothyroidism and has low radioactive iodine uptake.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes postpartum thyroiditis from Graves disease.

gaps.concept: Suckling reduces hypothalamic dopamine, increasing prolactin; prolactin suppresses GnRH and can delay ovulation.
gaps.why_tested: Explains the hormone pattern behind lactational amenorrhea.

gaps.concept: An unsensitized Rh-negative mother receives anti-D immune globulin after delivering an Rh-positive infant to prevent alloimmunization.
gaps.why_tested: Tests postpartum prevention of Rh hemolytic disease in a future pregnancy.
